reading.visual_notes: All 31 own pages and 26 primary pages rendered and viewed. No illegible notation, clipped code or displaced table found. Exact source formulas and the J2 printed-body exclusions were checked in the renders. Primary images remain private.

common_theory_review.reason: Transitive action type is the conjugacy class of a stabilizer; the core intersection gives the kernel. Equivariant permutations give normalizer quotients and wreath factors. Faithfulness is explicitly needed for the normalizer-to-Aut(A) sequence. No splitting is asserted.
Ambient equivalence of points lying over the same base object automatically lies in its stabilizer. Translation supplies every selected fiber; this works for nonfaithful and infinite actions.

Exact top support is invariant. At each fixed point the interval Mobius sum is exactly its top-support indicator; Burnside is applied to that invariant top-support subset of each actual stabilizer fiber. Individual support sublevel sets need not be invariant. Empty exact-support fibers contribute zero.

If Dz=az then involutivity and commutation imply a squared fixes z. An odd period expresses a as a power of its square on z, contradicting absence of fixed points. The field and inversion applications check each premise.

The anchored product test proves a common representative by induction; the geometric realization uses flag transitivity on each pair as well as on individual types. Right-coset conventions are consistent.

The nontrivial chamber stabilizer is preserved. Generated-subgroup intersections identify every residue; typed Helly provides flags and chamber completion. Residue generation gives connectedness. Firmness, RWPRI, local two-transitivity and rank-two partial-linearity/digon tests are stated separately.

RWPRI supplies a maximal deletion, so induction reaches each target. Ambient transporters and normalizer orbits enumerate all actual overgroups. Stabilizing the old tuple pointwise can only leave duplicates, which the final equivalence test removes. Strict joins give a finite chain bound, and every anchor actually certifies an empty next level.

applications.L066: Checked the complete orbit-multiplicity classification and faithfulness condition; reversal and parity formulas are all-degree written arguments. Full-automorphism degree-six fusion and polyhedron classification use the exhaustive required program. The source proof of Lemma 3.3 is repaired without changing its conclusion; Remark 3.4 remains endpoint-only, and Theorem 4.4 has its regular-polyhedron context.
applications.L074: Checked the normalized marking, canonical subfield position, generation, all intersection identities, rank/existence, duality and exact nested-formula equivalence. Suzuki/Luneburg group structure and finite-field automorphism theory are retained. The counting conclusion does not follow merely from bounded field examples. Broader background lemmas are marked retained or unused as specified.
applications.L104: Checked the exact six geometric axioms, arbitrary Borel subgroup recognition, maximal augmentation, subgroup transport, all-ranks termination and equivalence under the full ambient automorphism group/type permutations. The exact complete subgroup catalogue and GAP algorithms remain retained. Printed diagrams, full Aut/Cor and doubling assertions are excluded.

computational_review.witness_reproducibility: Fresh GAP output may use different printed generating lists. An independent semantic comparison verifies exact equality of all 170 panel/parabolic subgroups and all 30 Borel IDs/orders; two changed-data controls reject. Counts alone were not used as evidence of witness equality.
computational_review.code_appendix: All eight complete mathematical programs are included; exact nonspace inclusion in the printed appendix is verified. The two complete execution drivers are separately bound. No program is pruned.

formal_review.actual_scope: Fiber equivalence is formalized for one selected base orbit, including injectivity and surjectivity of the actual quotient map. The disjoint union over base orbits remains written. The odd-period action theorem and abstract centralizer rank obstruction are proved under explicit hypotheses.
